channel.title: One More Week
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "One More Week" - A backpack that allows its owner to live for one week, but at the cost of someone else's life.

item.content:encoded:

Here's some crit:

Central Narrative:

My main concern here is the execution of your narrative, you claim this is an SCP article, yet this appears to lean more towards being a tale. How is all this information portrayed in the article? Interviews, journals, casually in the description, where is it? You mention that there will be an interview but nothing about its contents.

clumsiness on the part of the retrieving agents has let the backpack claim them.

Are these not highly trained and briefed MTF Agents? They're not ones to simply inconveniently fuck up.

backpack is frequently found alone

I imagine a lot of these instances happen while the kid is hitchhiking and he suddenly bursts out bleeding in a car, or while working "odd jobs" or while riding the bus.

This:

even just grabbing the backpack is sufficient

Contradicts this:

Once someone finds and opens the backpack

And this:

Once opened the person opening it is transformed

Frankly, it seems like you have a generally good idea of the story but have no idea how you plan on presenting it in a digestible way to the reader. I'd like to see you expand on the execution side of things and fix some of the plot holes I pointed out.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) Again, you guys do things weird here. Most people aren't used to the whole "edit the original document every time a change is made"; it's normally assumed you would read the entire thread. Even a bullpen would consider every detail and then make changes; making piecemeal corrections tends to dilute the overall product.

Something that takes getting used to. Note that the original statement has yet again been edited.

2) By the same token, there are only so many details that you can put into 400 words, and I've seen that limit enforced for even going a few words over (I'm currently at 395, in case you're curious). Note carefully that I'm not arguing for a greater word count or that I don't see a reason for that limitation (even seeing as few abuses as I have of that here, it's hard not to see the wisdom therein), just saying that if you put a limit you need to make allowances for it.

As a writer. you just can't always make allowances for every sniggling detail, and sometimes you need to make a decision between making a complicated concept clear and delineating the relationship with The Foundation; which would you prefer as a reviewer?

Yeah, it's a jerk point, but if you want the best possible SCPs you need to make allowances that you may be missing some information you see as mandatory in order to better elaborate other information.

Also, as the body evaporates, there's no crime scene; that also gives it the appearance of an abandoned backpack after a death. The Foundation tries to grab it when it pops up, and a couple of Foundation agents have been lost to the backpack because they ignored parts of the containment process. Thus. while it's easy to track via the IP address of wherever Page logs in, they can't always send someone to retrieve it, especially as they need to do so in less than an hour.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Hey, brought in by request so lets see what we have.

Let's look at the SCP itself first. It seems like a fairly interesting concept with how his spirit lives on through the backpack and then imprints upon whomever opens it. But how do we know about the properties of the SCP if it was never tested? More so, is there any reason people keep buying a used backpack? Especially if the SCP dies with it on at the end of it, the backpack could be submitted to police evidence, destroyed, thrown in the garbage, or just never to be found. I would figure out a way to cover this plot hole that you have so that it's better understood how it gets passed on.

As for the Narrative, I have to echo what is said above. This definitely seems more suited for a tale as there is no mention of the Foundation involved. Rather you focus on the SCP itself and its journey, instead of how its contained. This would allow more creativity in terms of how you write the article and express the emotions of the SCP itself. It would also help explain how we know all these details about the SCP despite it not being in Foundation custody. I would suggest a tale either in the form of journal entries or just from the perspective of the SCP itself for what you have. Otherwise, this needs a serious overhaul to make it match an article. Best of luck.

Read: In most forums, you are actively discouraged from contacting mods except in major emergencies, while here it's par for the course.

I think there's a misunderstanding here—not all reviewers are moderators, and not all moderators are reviewers.

Since one of the main complaints we noted from reviewers was that authors would often ignore feedback unless they asked for it specifically, there was an attempt to shift focus towards authors reaching out to reviewers first to both familiarize themselves with how to ask/whom to ask, as well as confirming that there was an interest in continuing with the idea, rather than making the thread and then never responding to it.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) It's generally assumed that if your soul is used for the basis of an SCP that you died at some point. Otherwise, it can get rather awkward.

You really can't assume anything with anomalies. There are a number of items in the archives that involve this sort of thing, and it does indeed get awkward. That is a good thing for narrative purposes. SCP-3009 for instance revolves around a situation where the Foundation can't figure out whether one, both, or neither of a pair are the original person. There are anomalies that involve things like ambiguous duplication of a person obliviously living an otherwise normal life elsewhere, and others where it's implied that the anomaly involves an afterimage or reflection of a person and their desires at a certain moment in their lives.

The fact that this is a Philosophy student opens up some really cool opportunities on that front that I'd HIGHLY recommend embracing and running with. The meaning of "self" when we all shed identities over time, the search for truth and meaning, what constitutes a fulfilling life, whether there's any real value in contemplating paths not taken… These are are all long-standing philosophical topics that get extremely relevant to this anomaly if in 1989 Charles Anton Page changed his major from philosophy to business and is currently employed as a Junior Partner at a minor accounting firm in Oakland.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

My biggest concerns with this SCP are twofold:

1. The entire proposal is extremely focussed on what the SCP is to the point where you don't even mention the PoV characters at all (i.e., the Foundation).

2. There's no real growth or change over it.

The first is my general sign that a tale from the perspective of the SCP might be more interesting than a SCP article, in that, if you think the SCPs internal life and what happens to them is the most interesting aspect of the story, it's generally best to tell the story from that perspective so you don't have to rely on the SCP telling the Foundation what's up. It's also generally a good idea if you don't have a strong thing for the Foundation to be trying to do because it means you don't have to worry about questions like 'why are the Foundation doing this'.

The second is a bigger concern: at the end of the day, you're trying to tell a story, and they're fundamentally characterised by things happening and like, characters changing or the situation they're in changing or w/e, and at the moment, it just feels…like you have a very generic overview of how this works without a clear like, end goal in mind? E.g., the SCP doesn't grow emotionally, they don't strive to overcome anything, there's not even any specific events mentioned; and I just really want to see something more concrete using this, y'know?

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
1) His memory is basically a sliding scale; he remembers most of what he's encountered but he has problems with time (so he could place the events in order but not associate those events with a specific time). He also forgets that he dies; he has no idea that he's an anomaly or that he's only alive a week at a time now. He just has an urgency to get things done as quickly as possible.

2) He's not an agent of any GOI. In fact, it was only someone noting the dates and locations of his blog posts that happened to correlate to some missing people that the Foundation even had a clue he existed. (Given the nature of anomalies, I don't see it as a major stretch that the Foundation tracks when people go missing.) While he could theoretically be a decent operative for a GOI, the limitations on his memories make him more of a liability, and he couldn't be used as a reliable means to eliminate someone as you would need to guarantee that the person would a) pick the pack up, and b) would be the person to encounter the pack.

3) The transformation requires possession of the backpack and takes about three hours. The transformation could theoretically be reversed if the person stopped carrying the backpack after an hour or two; the biological template would then reassert itself. After that, it's too late. When the transformation is complete, he gains some of their skills (but they usually only last through the current incarnation) and the person's biometrics (such as fingerprints) but loses the bulk of their memories.

item.title: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Urban Legend

Page Layout: Standard description, some interview

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a beaten backpack with UC, Santa Cruz, patches on it. Once opened the person opening it is transformed into a clone of the original owner, who then returns to exploring the continental United States. He also writes about his experiences about his personal growth along the way, which helps pay his way.

Central Narrative: In 1989 Charles Anton Page decided to drop out of college and explore America; he felt trapped and needed to run away. He quickly adopted a "one week at a time" philosophy. A year, he was robbed and left for dead, and would eventually succumb to his wounds. The body was never recovered. His backpack, and the contents therein, were pawned at a local pawn shop. Someone bought the backpack, and over the next few hours was transformed into a virtual clone of Page, but without the knowledge of his death or that he was leading an extended life.

+ show block
– hide block

He is able to live for one week (168 hours) at a time before copies of the wounds that killed him appear on his body, and he then quickly succumbs to them. Once someone finds and opens the backpack, he is yet again allowed to live for another week, but with the usual memory lapse.

While he has adapted to the modern world somewhat (he writes a blog instead of magazine articles), he is still driven to explore the continental United States. He just does it one week at a time.

Hook/Attention Grabber: A basic urban legend about a youth cut short but still trying to find a way to accomplish his dream of exploring the United States through a mix of odd jobs, bus tickets, and hitchhiking, one week at a time.

Additional Notes: The body disintegrates upon death, leaving no body; this means that backpack is frequently found alone. Also, once the backpack has been taken into possession, the transformation begins; even just grabbing the backpack is sufficient. At that point the person is stuck with the backpack. Also, the backpack was in Foundation possession at one point but a GOC raid ended up in the backpack being freed (the person who took the backpack didn't get rid o it soon enough); while The Foundation does make attempts to reclaim the backpack, clumsiness on the part of the retrieving agents has let the backpack claim them.
